transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Maya (NebulaTech Head of ML), Tom (Infra), Priya (Product), Luis (CTO)

Summary (auto): scope POC capacity, define reserved vs burst strategy, bench metrics, timeline.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Samir, AE on the Redwood team.
00:12 Maya: hi, Maya here, thanks. we're trying to validate cost/latency trade offs for our chat agent, mostly public-facing.
00:20 Jules: Jules, SE — i'll own the benchmarks and the infra checklist. can you share the typical QPS and percent tail you care about?
00:32 Maya: right now in prod we see 20 rps average, spikes to 180 for short bursts, p95 latency target for user-facing is 600ms, p99 is sort of soft target, we really care about cost per conversation.
00:50 Tom: infra constraints: we've got a VPC with strict egress, need VPC peering or private link. keys via our KMS.
01:05 Samir: great, so for the POC we usually recommend a reserved baseline to cover your steady state, then burst nodes for peak. we can reserve GPUs (we call dedicated pools) and enable autoscale for bursts.
01:22 Maya: what's the typical reserve to burst ratio? and how does fallback work if burst not available?
01:30 Jules: good q. typical approach: reserve about 1.5x your average throughput in GPU capacity to hit p95, then allow burst up to 5-8x with pre-warmed instances or fast spin-up depending on region. fallback policy: if we can't allocate larger GPU or scaled replicas we automatically route to a compatible smaller model (quantized variant) or to hosted low-cost endpoints with graceful degradation settings — e.g., shorter context, smaller model.
02:05 Luis: that fallback worries me from product perspective, how do we avoid user-visible regressions?
02:12 Jules: the idea is canary test and synthetic benchmarks — also we define success criteria in terms of acceptable QA metrics. fallback should only be used for brief intervals and we can annotate responses with reduced fidelity flags. for the POC we can simulate a failover to measure user impact.
02:36 Priya: success criteria from product: p95 < 600ms for 95% of traffic, cost per convo below $0.08, and no more than 1% fallback events during business hours.
02:50 Samir: good concrete numbers. Jules, for capacity sizing we need a sample workload trace — ideally 7 days of traffic — and typical prompt length and max tokens.
03:02 Maya: we'll upload that, we have 30-60 token prompts and mean output about 120 tokens.
03:10 Tom: also note 50% of requests come from mobile with weaker connections, so tail latency matters.
03:20 Jules: ok, for benchmarking we'll run: 1) steady state p95/p99 latency at reserved size, 2) burst ramp tests to peak QPS with pre-warmed nodes, 3) cold start scale tests, 4) fallback-routing exercise. we'll capture tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates.
03:45 Maya: how long do benchmarks take?
03:48 Jules: each scenario ~2-4 hours, full suite ~12 hours. we usually run them overnight.
03:56 Samir: pricing for reserved capacity: for POC we offer a short-term commit (4 weeks) with possibility to convert to Dedicated. baseline reserved suggestion: 4 A100-ish equivalents to target your steady 20 rps and handle p95. bursts add 6 GPUs ephemeral (burst pool) depending on workload — we'll refine after we see your traces.
04:20 Maya: are those exact A100 numbers or quantized equivalents?
04:24 Jules: depends on model size and quantization. if you run 70B quantized we can fit more QPS per GPU. we'll propose two profiles: conservative (float16 large) and optimized (int8/quant) with projected cost numbers.
04:40 Tom: how quickly can bursts spin up? customer regions?
04:44 Jules: cold spinup can be 2-5 minutes for new nodes; warm pre-warmed burst instances can be sub-30s. region depends, we'll map your region to nearest Redwood pool.
04:58 Luis: SLA expectations for POC?
05:02 Samir: POC not SLA-backed but we'll aim for engineering support; Dedicated contracts get SLAs. for the POC we'll provide 24/7 alerting and a dedicated engineer during benchmark days.
05:18 Priya: timeline — we want results in 6 weeks, is that feasible?
05:22 Samir: yes: week 0-1: sample traces and success criteria, week 2: infra setup and smoke tests, week 3: run benchmarks, week 4-5: analyze and iterate, week 6: final report and recommendation.
05:36 Maya: what about audit logs and data retention? our security team needs logs and to prove no customer data leaves the VPC.
05:45 Tom: also need KMS integration and SOC2 details.
05:50 Samir: we'll share the security pack — SAML/SSO docs, SOC2, KMS, audit log retention. for VPC we support peering or private endpoints and on-prem options in sensitive cases.
06:04 Jules: one more: we'll capture KV cache hit rates — that impacts cost a lot for chat workloads. if your prefix reuse is high caching reduces GPU token work significantly.
06:18 Maya: we have about 35% prefix reuse on average.
06:22 Jules: cool that's helpful. for POC sizing that reduces baseline GPU need by ~20% conservative estimate.
06:30 Samir: ok next steps recap: Maya to upload traces and prompt sets; Jules will send benchmark runbook; Samir will send POC proposal and provisional pricing; Tom to confirm networking/KMS scope; schedule kickoff week of May 4.
06:48 Maya: sounds good.
06:50 Luis: thanks everyone.
06:52 Samir: thanks, we'll follow up with docs and dates. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps and imperfect proper nouns; speaker attribution mostly correct but may have minor mislabels.
